lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: building a contingency for the main plan

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic building a contingency for the main plan task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Using either a plan the learner already built earlier in the course or a provided example plan (equal credit either way), the learner identifies the one step most likely to fail and writes an 'if this fails, then—' contingency branch with a clear trigger for when to activate it.
safetyNotes: Using a provided example plan instead of a real personal one is fully acceptable and earns equal credit; nothing here requires disclosing a real personal plan's details.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Is one backup enough for this weak point, or does it need more than one? Why?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Weak-point identification: A specific, plausible weak point is identified with a clear reason. | Contingency specificity: The trigger is specific and recognizable in the moment. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write a contingency for the second most likely point of failure as well, and compare how the two contingencies differ.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic building a contingency for the main plan task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: building a contingency for the main plan worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Using either a plan the learner already built earlier in the course or a provided example plan (equal credit either way), the learner identifies the one step most likely to fail and writes an 'if this fails, then—' contingency branch with a clear trigger for when to activate it.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact building a contingency for the main plan decision or action.
Model move 2: Before identifying the weak point, predict what kind of failure is most common in plans like this one.
Model move 3: Identify the single most likely point of failure in your chosen plan.
Model check: Weak-point identification: A specific, plausible weak point is identified with a clear reason. | Contingency specificity: The trigger is specific and recognizable in the moment.

resources.title: building a contingency for the main plan action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for building a contingency for the main plan.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: building a contingency for the main plan coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Using either a plan the learner already built earlier in the course or a provided example plan (equal credit either way), the learner identifies the one step most likely to fail and writes an 'if this fails, then—' contingency branch with a clear trigger for when to activate it.
Coach direction: Before identifying the weak point, predict what kind of failure is most common in plans like this one.
Learner prompt: In general, what kind of thing most often causes a plan like this to fail — bad timing, missing a resource, or something else? Why do you think that?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: building a contingency for the main plan complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Identify the single most likely point of failure in your chosen plan.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named one specific step in the plan as the most likely point of failure.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I explained why that step, specifically, is the weakest one.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: building a contingency for the main plan minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Is one backup enough for this weak point, or does it need more than one? Why?
Success checks: Weak-point identification: A specific, plausible weak point is identified with a clear reason. | Contingency specificity: The trigger is specific and recognizable in the moment.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: building a contingency for the main plan supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional building a contingency for the main plan condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Weak-point identification: A specific, plausible weak point is identified with a clear reason. | Contingency specificity: The trigger is specific and recognizable in the moment..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: Using either a plan the learner already built earlier in the course or a provided example plan (equal credit either way), the learner identifies the one step most likely to fail and writes an 'if this fails, then—' contingency branch with a clear trigger for when to activate it.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: In general, what kind of thing most often causes a plan like this to fail — bad timing, missing a resource, or something else? Why do you think that?
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Weak-point identification: A specific, plausible weak point is identified with a clear reason.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

simulationRoute.title: building a contingency for the main plan — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the building a contingency for the main plan task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Is one backup enough for this weak point, or does it need more than one? Why?
observableCriteria: Weak-point identification: A specific, plausible weak point is identified with a clear reason.
Contingency specificity: The trigger is specific and recognizable in the moment.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Weak-point identification: A specific, plausible weak point is identified with a clear reason. | Contingency specificity: The trigger is specific and recognizable in the moment.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
